messages:
Acme Integrations: Hey team — since yesterday morning our embeddings calls to /v1/embeddings have intermittent 2–5s tail latency spikes even though median is ~120ms. Started after we switched to dynamic batching + max_batch_size=64. No errors returned, just slow responses.
Maria L.: Thanks for the report — can you share a request_id for a slow trace and whether this is hosted/dedicated?
Acme Integrations: hosted, region=us-west1. Example request_id: rq_3895012345_ab12. Happened ~12:17 UTC. Payloads are mixed: some 64-dim vectors and some 1024-dim text->embeds (we call text-embedding-ada-ish).
Alex P.: Mixing models/dims on the same route would normally be rejected — are you routing different models to same embeddings endpoint?
Acme Integrations: We pin model=name:open-embed-1024 in the client. But some legacy clients still send upsampled small arrays for testing. No explicit model switch.
Jin K.: Do you have any server-side logs? If you can paste the batcher debug for rq_3895012345_ab12 that helps. Typical symptom: coalesce window flushes small partial batches and one request waits for KV caching or flush.
Acme Integrations: Paste from our side (truncated):
```
[12:17:03] batcher: receive req rq_3895012345_ab12 size=1024
[12:17:03] batcher: coalesce_window_ms=20 current_batch_size=3
[12:17:03] batcher: max_batch_size=64
[12:17:05] batcher: coalesce timeout expired -> flush batch size=3
[12:17:05] runtime: allocate kv cache -> miss -> warmup 180ms
[12:17:06] runtime: kernel select -> compiled quantized path
[12:17:07] response sent 2200ms
```
Maria L.: That log is useful — shows coalesce timeout + KV cache warmup contributing. Does the platform show model variant evictions around that time?
SRE Oncall: Checked infra — no node evictions. But we saw a spike in KV miss latency ~180ms across worker pool at 12:17 UTC, correlated with a small batch flush pattern.
Alex P.: Two likely causes: 1) small/large request mixing causing frequent partial flushes, 2) cold KV entries when a variant is selected (e.g., dynamic quantization path). Workarounds: increase coalesce_window_ms slightly or enable "prefer_partial":true so small requests don't stall large ones, or use routing tags to keep homogeneous dims together.
Acme Integrations: Can you give concrete config we should try? Our current dynamic batching config: `max_batch_size: 64`, `coalesce_window_ms: 20`, `allow_partial_batches: false`
Jin K.: Try this minimal tweak: `allow_partial_batches: true`, `coalesce_window_ms: 10`, and add client header `X-Embedding-Dim: 1024` so routing can group. If you can't add header, group by API key per client or pin smaller batchers.
Support Bot: FYI — there were transient rate-limit events for api-key:acme_*** at 12:16:45 but they were soft-limited (429s < 0.1%). Not likely main cause but keep an eye.
Acme Integrations: Applying changes now to test. Any quick repro we can run to simulate mix?
Maria L.: Yes — run a loop that sends 1 large text embed every 50ms and 5 tiny test embeds concurrently to simulate interleaving. Example cURL: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024","input":"some long text..."}' &
  for j in {1..5}; do
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
      -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024","input":[0.1,0.2]}' &
  done
  sleep 0.05
done
```
This should reproduce partial flushes and tail jitter.
Acme Integrations: Test started — will report back in ~10m. Appreciate the config tips. :thumbsup:
Alex P.: If tail persists after the config change, we'll escalate to runtime team to inspect kernel selection latencies and KV cold-start patterns. Also include any demo traces (span IDs) and capture `batcher.metrics` around the window.
Acme Integrations: Update after 12m — with `allow_partial_batches=true` and `coalesce_window_ms=10` median stayed ~150ms and tail spikes reduced to ~600ms (was 2–5s). Looks much better.
Maria L.: Great — sounds like a successful mitigation. If you want zero-tail, we can recommend dedicating a lane (dedicated consumer) for large embeddings or enable prewarmed KV for that model.
Acme Integrations: We'll accept this for now and revisit dedicated routing next quarter. Thanks for the quick help!
SRE Oncall: Marking as resolved for now. If you see recurrence, file a new thread with traces and we'll reopen. :white_check_mark:
